coverage.evidence: package.json:45 names the exact version "1.0.0-next.18" with no range operator, installed with npm install -E so no caret was introduced. The lockfile is committed and carries a fresh integrity hash for peer-ai-eslint-config and for the two packages it depends on, peer-ai-standards and peer-ai-workflow, all three moving next.16 to next.18 together.

No dependency is added; one devDependency moves two patch releases within the same pre-release line, to stay level with the Peer AI version the config, the MCP registration and the CI gate all name. The reason is in the commit message and the pull request: three fixes this project hit today, each named.

Unchanged and still failing: nothing checks dependencies for vulnerabilities, on change or on a schedule. pr-checks.yml runs verify, the repo-rules guard and gitleaks; peer-ai.yml runs the gate; neither runs npm audit, there is no scheduled workflow and no dependency bot. npm audit at this commit reports the same 19 vulnerabilities as before this change - 5 critical, 8 high, 5 moderate, 1 low - all in the build and test toolchain, none in the shipped bundle, and none from the three packages this change moves. Carried forward from ITEM-9's report rather than restated as new.

coverage.reason: DEL-07 applies from production and nothing is deployed. The moved package is a devDependency read only by eslint.config.js; nothing it brings in reaches the browser bundle.

coverage.evidence: No .npmrc exists, so installs go to the default public registry, and all three moved packages resolve in package-lock.json to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with integrity hashes. The project publishes nothing under a private scope: @mizaniya/core is a workspace package resolved from packages/core by path, so dependency confusion has no surface.

coverage.reason: DEL-10 applies from production and nothing is released. package-lock.json is a complete list of every direct and indirect dependency with its version and registry, which is the rule's substance; a generated bill of materials belongs with the deployment work.

coverage.evidence: Read from each installed package's own metadata: peer-ai-eslint-config, peer-ai-standards and peer-ai-workflow all declare license MIT at next.18, as they did at next.16. MIT imposes nothing on this repository's PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 licensing, and all three are devDependencies, so none is distributed with the product.

None of the three runs code at install time: their package.json scripts are build and generate only, no preinstall, install or postinstall hook, read from the installed copies. None is abandoned - all three were published today as part of the same release line. None is a look-alike: they are the packages this project already depended on, moving between versions of the same line. The one install script npm warned about, unrs-resolver's postinstall, comes from eslint-import-resolver-typescript, predates this change, and npm declined to run it.

findings.title: Nothing checks dependencies for vulnerabilities, and 5 critical advisories stand
findings.evidence: A vulnerability published tomorrow in a package already installed here would be found by nobody, since nothing runs on a schedule and no bot is configured. npm audit at this commit: 19 vulnerabilities, 5 critical, 8 high, all in the build and test toolchain - eslint-plugin-boundaries through handlebars and micromatch, tailwindcss through chokidar and fast-glob, vite, vitest through tinypool - none in the shipped bundle and none from this change. Three of the criticals were published within six days against code already installed here, which is the rule's own argument. Raised first on ITEM-9 and unchanged by this item; the owner has asked for it to be solved next.
findings.fix: Add npm audit to pr-checks.yml and a scheduled workflow that runs it daily, with a severity threshold that fails the build and a time to fix per severity. Separate the dev-only tree from the shipped one in what blocks, so a build-tool advisory does not block a merge that ships nothing.

summary: Pass at the project's blocking level, with the same high finding carried forward. The change itself is clean: exact pin, committed lockfile with fresh integrity hashes, MIT read from the packages, public registry with integrity, no install scripts, reason recorded. DEL-03 still fails for the same reason as on ITEM-9 - nothing watches dependencies - and the audit numbers are unchanged by this bump.
